items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S532

SPONSOR: PERSAUD
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the executive law, in relation to minimum standards for
code enforcement personnel

 
PURPOSE:

Relates to minimum standards for code enforcement personnel

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

This bill amends the authority of the secretary of state to promulgate
rules and regulations regarding code enforcement by making the issuance
mandatory instead of permissive. It additionally creates a timeline for
completion of the mandatory training for code enforcement personnel and
increases the annual continuing education required to maintain certif-
ication. Finally, the bill prohibits continued employment as code
enforcement personnel where the individual's certification has been
suspended or revoked unless the person has received an extension to
become active by the Secretary of State.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

On August 5, 2019, the Committees on Investigations and Government Oper-
ations and Housing, Construction, and Community Development, respective-
ly, released a report on code enforcement in New York State. The inves-
tigation concluded the lack of prioritization of code enforcement in
municipalities across the State is significantly contributing to the
culture of poor compliance that ultimately endangers the lives of resi-
dents and first responders.

The report found that the training and certification requirements of
code enforcement personnel were inadequate. It recommended creating a
defined period of time for code enforcement personnel to finish their
training and obtain certification, increasing the annual continuing
education hours, and prohibiting employment where code enforcement
personnel has lost their certification. This bill incorporates each of
those recommendations.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: S7291 Referred to Governmental Operations

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become a law.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 82 Chapter 797
 
        MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 532-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to minimum standards
        for code enforcement personnel"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill enhances training requirements and provides for the enforce-
ment  of  those  requirements  for  building safety instructors and code
enforcement officials. It also shortens the time period by  which  these
officials  must complete basic training requirements subsequent to their
appointment, with exceptions available for good cause.
 
  In addition, this bill increases the training hours required for annu-
al recertification for building safety instructors and code  enforcement
officials. However, the law already requires these officials to complete
some  of the most rigorous recertification requirements of professionals
in the State. Therefore, I have reached an agreement with  the  Legisla-
ture  to  maintain  the  number of training hours required for recertif-
ication.  This will ensure that the recertification process is effective
yet not overly burdensome.
 
  Based on this agreement with the Legislature, I  am  pleased  to  sign
this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Relates to minimum standards for code enforcement personnel; requires the secretary of state to promulgate rules and regulations in relation to minimum standards for code enforcement personnel including requirements for training.
